cli.help.stats:
Usage: {command} stats [--by step|version|command|model|phase|page|actor] [--since <version>] [--csv] [--json]

Shows the project's production statistics, read from usage/<version>.jsonl: the time spent in each block (setup, facts and each source, capture and each part — navigate, actions, wait, mask, shot, encode, compare —, generation, translation, update, build, checks), the tokens and models of the agents, per version of the application. Every command appends its timings there when the project has a usage/ folder (DOC_KIT_STATS=0 turns it off).

  --by       grouping (default: step; its parts are listed under each step)
  --since    only versions from this one on
  --csv      every line as CSV, for a spreadsheet
  --json     the totals as JSON

Any command shows its own timings with --profile.

cli.help.changes:
Usage: {command} changes [--since <git ref>] [--output <file>] [--record] [--json]

What changed in the application since a reference (default HEAD): the facts files as committed at <ref> against the ones on disk now — routes and their authentication, tables and columns, environment variables, dependencies and versions, security findings, secrets (files and rules, never values), AI agent instruction files, import cycles, number of tests. Run {command} facts first. Writes {work}/changes.md (ready for a pull request comment or the release notes) and {work}/changes.json, and prints the Markdown.

  --since    the git reference to compare with (a commit, a tag, origin/main)
  --output   write the Markdown there instead of {work}/changes.md
  --record   also keep them in changes/<documented version>.json (commit it): the ::changes directive shows every recorded version in the site, most recent first

cli.help.hooks:
Usage: {command} hooks install | uninstall | status [--app <dir>]

Local updates without CI: git hooks in the application's repository (post-merge after a git pull, post-checkout after a branch switch) that run {command} facts then {command} sync from the documentation project, quietly, never failing git, zero tokens. An existing hook is kept: the kit only adds, or removes, its own block. The hooks folder comes from git (core.hooksPath and worktrees are honoured).

  --app   the application's folder (default: app.dir)

cli.help.record:
Usage: {command} record <route> [--id <id>] [--force]

Writes a capture plan entry by doing it: opens Playwright's recorder on the application (signed in with the saved session), you click, type and choose what the capture must show, then close the browser. The steps become captures/plans/<id>.mjs (route and actions); the lines that cannot be translated are kept as comments. Add the zones and the frame, then check with {command} capture <id> --preview.

The recorder is a normal browser, not the read-only capture: refused when capture.target is "production" and on a capture.forbidden route.

  --id      the capture id (default: from the route)
  --force   replace an existing plan file
